# rcol

`rcol` is an R client for the [Catalogue of
Life](https://www.catalogueoflife.org) via the
[ChecklistBank](https://www.checklistbank.org) API
(<https://api.checklistbank.org>). It allows you to verify and match
scientific names, retrieve hierarchical classifications, look up
datasets, taxa, synonyms, vernacular names, and geographic
distributions, and run ChecklistBank parsers — against **any** public
dataset in ChecklistBank or the latest Catalogue of Life release. It is
modelled on the conventions of
[`rgbif`](https://docs.ropensci.org/rgbif/) and
[`taxadb`](https://docs.ropensci.org/taxadb/).

> **Note on Origin & Architectural Evolution**: This package builds upon
> the original [`rcol` project by Catalogue of
> Life](https://github.com/CatalogueOfLife/rcol)
> (<https://catalogueoflife.github.io/rcol/>). This version introduces
> substantial architectural enhancements to simplify scientific
> workflows, including:
>
> - **Direct Scientific Name Support**: Pass scientific names directly
>   (e.g., `"Panthera leo"` or `"Werneria nubigena"`) to downstream
>   functions without needing prior manual ID lookups.
> - **Vectorized Multi-Species Queries**: Seamlessly pass character
>   vectors of multiple species (e.g.,
>   `c("Werneria nubigena", "Panthera leo")`) and receive clean,
>   concatenated tidy data frames.
> - **Distribution Traceability**: Multi-species distributions include
>   `input_row` and `scientific_name`, preserving their association with
>   the original input.
> - **Clean Name Verification**:
>   [`col_check_name()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_resolve_name.md)
>   returns an essential 9-column resolution summary showing accepted
>   names, status, and IDs.
> - **Flexible Classification Extraction**:
>   [`col_classification()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/col_shortcuts.md)
>   supports both Long format and Wide format (`wide = TRUE`).

There are two parallel families of functions:

- **`col_*()`** convenience functions that target the **latest extended
  Catalogue of Life release** (`"3LXR"`). On first use, the release key
  is pinned in session
  ([`col_key()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/col_key.md)),
  ensuring long-running jobs are never disrupted by mid-session release
  updates. Use
  [`col_refresh()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/col_refresh.md)
  to re-pin.
- **`clb_*()`** universal low-level functions that accept an explicit
  `dataset =` argument (e.g., `"COL25"`, `2099`) to query any dataset in
  ChecklistBank.

## Installation

Install the package from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("PaulESantos/rcol")

# or
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("PaulESantos/rcol")
```

Documentation is published at <https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/>.

## Quick start

### 1. Name Verification & Matching

``` r

library(rcol)

# High-level clean verification (9 columns) for 1 or multiple species
col_check_name(c("Werneria nubigena", "Panthera leo", "Schinus molle"))

# Detailed matching against the latest Catalogue of Life release
col_match("Panthera leo")

# Disambiguate with rank and nomenclatural code
col_match("Abies alba", rank = "species", code = "botanical")

# See all candidate matches (homonyms), not just the best one
col_match_verbose("Oenanthe")

# Match many names at once in parallel
col_match_checklist(c("Panthera leo", "Bufo bufo", "Abies alba"))
```

To match against a specific dataset instead of the latest COL release,
use the `clb_*()` form with a `dataset =` key or alias:

``` r

clb_match("Felis catus", dataset = "COL25")          # 2025 annual release
clb_match("Macrocystis pyrifera", dataset = 2099)    # public dataset by key
```

### 2. Classification, Synonyms, Vernaculars & Distribution

The following lookup functions accept scientific names, IDs, vectors, or
match result tables:

``` r

# Hierarchical classification in Wide or Long format
col_classification("Schinus molle", wide = TRUE)

# Synonyms for 1 or multiple species
col_synonyms(c("Werneria nubigena", "Panthera leo"))

# Vernacular / common names with species association (scientific_name column)
col_vernacular(c("Werneria nubigena", "Panthera leo"))

# Geographic distribution in tidy format
col_distribution(c("Werneria nubigena", "Schinus molle"))

# Details of a name usage
col_usage("Panthera leo")
```

### 3. Tree Navigation & Search

``` r

# Walk the COL tree roots (Domains / Realms)
roots <- col_tree()

# Get direct child species under a genus
col_children("Panthera")

# Full-text search with rank and status filters
col_usage_search("Panthera", rank = "species", status = "accepted")
```

### 4. Parsers

``` r

# Parse a scientific name into its atomic components
clb_parse_name("Abies alba Mill. var. alpina")
```

## Catalogue of Life Releases

The Catalogue of Life is published in two cadences (monthly and annual)
and two flavours (base and extended `XR`). Dataset-scoped `clb_*()`
functions take a `dataset =` argument; helpful aliases resolve to the
latest of each:

``` r

clb_col_release("monthly")                  # "3LR"   latest monthly base
clb_col_release("monthly", extended = TRUE) # "3LXR"  latest monthly extended
clb_col_release("annual")                   # e.g. "COL25"

clb_usage_search("Felidae", dataset = "COL25")
```

## Batch results and failures

[`col_match_checklist()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/col_shortcuts.md)
and
[`clb_match_checklist()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_match_checklist.md)
keep one row per input and preserve input columns with a `verbatim_`
prefix. Inspect `match` and `error` before interpreting the results:

| `match` | `error` | Meaning                                       |
|---------|---------|-----------------------------------------------|
| `TRUE`  | `NA`    | A matching usage was returned.                |
| `FALSE` | `NA`    | The request succeeded but no match was found. |
| `NA`    | Message | The request or response parsing failed.       |

``` r

batch <- col_match_checklist(c("Panthera leo", "Schinus molle"))
failed <- batch[is.na(batch$match), ]
unmatched <- batch[!is.na(batch$match) & !batch$match, ]
matched <- batch[!is.na(batch$match) & batch$match, ]
failed[c("verbatim_name", "error")]
```

These per-row diagnostics apply to batch requests. Failures before
requests are submitted, such as resolving
[`col_key()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/col_key.md),
still raise an error. The simpler
[`col_check_name()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_resolve_name.md)
summary retains `match = NA` for failed rows but does not include the
`error` column; use
[`col_match_checklist()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/col_shortcuts.md)
when diagnosing failures.

## Distribution provenance and raw responses

For multiple inputs,
[`col_distribution()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_distribution.md)
includes `input_row` (the one-based position in the input),
`scientific_name`, and `area`. A species can have several rows after
splitting semicolon-separated areas. Species with no distribution
records contribute no rows, so use `input_row` rather than row position
to join results back to your input.

``` r

species <- c("Panthera leo", "Schinus molle")
distribution <- col_distribution(species)
distribution$queried_name <- species[distribution$input_row]

# Add status, gazetteer, remarks and reference metadata
col_distribution(species, full = TRUE)

# Resolve an ID or a verification result before formatting the classification
col_classification("4CGXP", wide = TRUE)
verified <- col_check_name("Schinus molle")
col_classification(verified, wide = TRUE)

# Keep nested API responses intact and aligned with each input
responses <- col_usage(species, .raw = TRUE)
responses[[1]]
```

For a single input, distribution output defaults to `area`;
`full = TRUE` also includes `scientific_name` and metadata. Usage,
classification, synonym, vernacular and distribution lookups with
multiple inputs and `.raw = TRUE` return a list of complete parsed
responses, including empty responses, instead of combining them into a
tibble. With one input, `.raw = TRUE` returns the single parsed
response. For classification, `.raw = TRUE` takes precedence over
`wide`.

When passing a result table to a taxon lookup, valid IDs are selected in
order from `accepted_id`, `usage_id`, and `id`, skipping missing or
empty values. Unresolved rows raise an error. Filter failed and
unmatched rows before passing a batch result to a downstream lookup.

## Building documentation and running tests

Online examples are displayed without execution when the README and
vignettes are built. This allows documentation builds without contacting
ChecklistBank. Unit tests run without API access; live integration tests
are opt-in and remain skipped on CRAN.

``` r

devtools::test()

# Run live integration tests in a development session with Internet access
withr::with_envvar(c(RCOL_LIVE_TESTS = "true"), devtools::test())

# Build and check the package, including its vignettes and PDF manual
devtools::check(cran = TRUE, manual = TRUE)
```

Documentation builds require Pandoc; the PDF manual also requires a
working LaTeX installation. These tools are separate from access to the
API.

## Configuration

The base URL defaults to the production API and can be redirected with
the `CLB_BASE_URL` environment variable:

``` r

Sys.setenv(CLB_BASE_URL = "https://api.dev.checklistbank.org")
```

## Citation

To cite `rcol` in publications, please use:

``` r

citation("rcol")
```

# Package index

## Name Verification and Matching (COL)

Core functions for scientific name matching, clean 9-column
verification, and homonym candidate inspection using the Catalogue of
Life extended release.

  [`clb_check_name()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_resolve_name.md)
  : Resolve and verify valid species names
- [`col_match()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/col_shortcuts.md)
  [`col_match_verbose()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/col_shortcuts.md)
  [`col_match_checklist()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/col_shortcuts.md)
  [`col_dataset()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/col_shortcuts.md)
  [`col_dataset_metrics()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/col_shortcuts.md)

## Universal ChecklistBank Interface (CLB)

Low-level complementary functions (`clb_*` family) for advanced queries
against any specific ChecklistBank dataset or historical COL release.

- [`clb_resolve_name()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_resolve_name.md)
  [`col_resolve_name()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_resolve_name.md)
  [`col_check_name()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_resolve_name.md)
  [`clb_check_name()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_resolve_name.md)
  : Resolve and verify valid species names
- [`clb_match()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_match.md)
  : Match a scientific name against a ChecklistBank dataset
- [`clb_match_checklist()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_match_checklist.md)
  : Match a checklist of names in bulk
- [`clb_match_verbose()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_match_verbose.md)
  : Match a name and return all candidate usages
- [`clb_classification()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_classification.md)
  : Classification hierarchy of a taxon
- [`clb_extract_classification()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_extract_classification.md)
  [`col_extract_classification()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_extract_classification.md)
  : Extract taxonomic classification from a match or usage result
- [`clb_synonyms()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_synonyms.md)
  : Synonyms of a taxon
- [`clb_vernacular()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_vernacular.md)
  : Vernacular (common) names
- [`clb_distribution()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_distribution.md)
  [`col_distribution()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_distribution.md)
  : Geographic distribution for a taxon
- [`clb_usage()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_usage.md)
  : Get a name usage (taxon or synonym) by id
- [`clb_usage_search()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_usage_search.md)
  [`clb_search()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_usage_search.md)
  : Full-text search of name usages
- [`clb_suggest()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_suggest.md)
  : Autocomplete suggestions for name usages
- [`clb_usage_metrics()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_usage_metrics.md)
  : Metrics for a taxon
- [`clb_tree()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_tree.md)
  : Navigate the taxonomic tree
- [`clb_children()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_children.md)
  : Direct children of a taxon
- [`clb_dataset()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_dataset.md)
  : Get dataset metadata
- [`clb_dataset_search()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_dataset_search.md)
  : Search datasets in ChecklistBank
- [`clb_dataset_metrics()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_dataset_metrics.md)
  : Dataset metrics
- [`clb_col_release()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_col_release.md)
  : Resolve a Catalogue of Life release
- [`clb_col_releases()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_col_releases.md)
  : List all Catalogue of Life releases
- [`clb_base_url()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_base_url.md)
  : The ChecklistBank API base URL

## ChecklistBank Parsers

Tools for parsing scientific names into atomic epithets and parsing
controlled values.

- [`clb_parse_name()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_parse_name.md)
  : Parse scientific names
- [`clb_parsers()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_parsers.md)
  : List the available ChecklistBank parsers
- [`clb_parse()`](https://paulesantos.github.io/rcol/reference/clb_parse.md)
  : Parse values with a ChecklistBank value parser
